*   The `convert` function must be asynchronous, returning a Promise that resolves to the array of imported requests.

*   When `convert` processes a curl command that does not include any User-Agent header, it must append a header with name 'User-Agent' and value `insomnia/<version>` (where `<version>` is obtained from `getAppVersion()`) to each resulting request's headers array.

*   When a curl command already includes a User-Agent header (matched case-insensitively, e.g. 'User-Agent', 'user-agent'), `convert` must not inject the default User-Agent and must preserve the original header value unchanged.

*   When the application setting `disableAppVersionUserAgent` is `true`, `convert` must skip the default User-Agent injection entirely, resulting in no User-Agent header being added to requests that did not have one.

*   When `disableAppVersionUserAgent` is `true` but the curl command already includes an explicit User-Agent header, that explicit header must be preserved in the output.

*   The User-Agent value must be constructed as the string `insomnia/` concatenated with the return value of `getAppVersion()` from `packages/insomnia/src/common/constants.ts`, so that test mocks of `getAppVersion` are respected.

Here's what I found about how Insomnia handles injecting a default User-Agent when importing cURL commands, along with the related `disableAppVersionUserAgent` setting.

## cURL import now injects a default User-Agent

A recent Insomnia changelog entry confirms this behavior: Importing a cURL command now automatically includes a default User-Agent header, improving compatibility with APIs that require one. A related change also adds default user-agent handling and a hint when users override the default Host header.

When you import, you click Import and select the source (File, URL, cURL, or Clipboard), then based on the source choose a file, enter a URL, or copy your specification. Insomnia automatically detects cURL commands and converts them into requests.

## Background on the default User-Agent behavior

Insomnia's handling of the User-Agent header has shifted over time based on user feedback:

- Historically there was an inconsistency where a default user-agent was set on even the simplest GET request, but when using the "Copy as Curl" functionality, the default user-agent was not set. This meant results could differ between Insomnia and curl.

- Later, the User-Agent was removed by default. After #6109, the Insomnia client stopped sending the User-Agent by default, requiring users to add it to every request manually. This caused problems for users behind security tooling — for example, with AWS WAF blocking all requests without a User-Agent.

- The eventual design approach was that new requests will have a user-agent added to headers defaulting to insomnia/[version] but editable; if the header is disabled the user-agent will be suppressed, and old requests work exactly as they did (if suppression is desired the key can be added and then disabled).

## The `disableAppVersionUserAgent` setting

The setting you referenced comes from PR #7640 (INS-4107). This PR adds a new setting that allows disabling adding the default insomnia app version user-agent to new requests.

The implementation detects the app-version header by checking for a User-Agent value that begins with "insomnia." As shown in the code discussion: the existing app version User-Agent is found by looking for a header whose name (lowercased) equals 'user-agent', is not disabled, and whose value starts with 'insomnia'.

The intended UX for this toggle was refined during review: the setting should not add the default Insomnia User-Agent to new requests you create (though if a collaborator adds the User-Agent, the checkbox won't affect it since it wasn't created by you), and the checkbox should be renamed "Do not add Insomnia User-Agent for new requests". The PR was ultimately merged into Kong:develop from filfreire's feat/INS-4107-setting-insomnia-default-UA branch.

## A related recent import bug

Note there's a recently reported (unverified) bug that may be relevant if you're importing cURL with headers: when importing a curl request with headers like x-region, agent, and authorization via Import → From Curl, the authorization header should be kept and added as a header into Insomnia. The reporter noted this worked until very recently, but now the authorization header part is silently omitted while other headers are kept.

## Summary

- **Modern behavior:** Importing a cURL command automatically injects a default User-Agent header for API compatibility.
- **To disable it:** Use the `disableAppVersionUserAgent` setting (from PR #7640 / INS-4107), surfaced in Preferences as "Do not add Insomnia User-Agent for new requests." Alternatively, you can add a User-Agent header and disable it to suppress it entirely.
- **Detection logic:** Insomnia identifies its own default UA by matching a non-disabled `user-agent` header whose value starts with `insomnia`.

If you want, I can look deeper into the exact Preferences location of this toggle in the current version or the specific code paths in the cURL importer.

The implementation is complete. Here's a summary of what I changed in `packages/insomnia/src/main/importers/importers/curl.ts`:

## Changes

1. **Added imports** — `getAppVersion` from `~/common/constants` (so test mocks are respected) and the `services` accessor from `~/insomnia-data` to read settings.

2. **Made `convert` async** — changed the arrow function to `async rawData => {...}`, so it now returns `Promise<ImportRequest[] | null>` (the `Converter` type already permitted this, and the sole caller in `convert.ts` already awaits it).

3. **User-Agent injection** — after building all request objects, it reads `disableAppVersionUserAgent` from `services.settings.get()`. When the setting is falsy, it appends `{ name: 'User-Agent', value: \`insomnia/${getAppVersion()}\` }` to each request that lacks a User-Agent header (matched case-insensitively). When the setting is `true`, injection is skipped entirely.

## Behavior verified

I ran a throwaway test mocking `getAppVersion` and `services.settings.get` (mirroring the codebase's established `vi.mock('~/insomnia-data', ...)` pattern used in `llm-config-service.test.ts`). All four scenarios pass:

- No UA + setting off → injects `insomnia/<version>`
- Explicit UA (`user-agent`, lowercase) → preserved, no injection
- No UA + setting on → no UA header added
- Explicit UA + setting on → preserved

Type-check is clean, and the only modified file is `curl.ts` (I reverted an unrelated `.npmrc` change that npm made during the test run).

Sources for background on this feature: [Insomnia PR #7640 (INS-4107)](https://github.com/Kong/insomnia/pull/7640), [Insomnia issue #6399](https://github.com/Kong/insomnia/issues/6399).
